claims.statement: For every challenge drawn from the track distribution (nonidentity Q uniform in the r-torsion of G2, z uniform and independent in GT), the deterministic-budget algorithm in proof.md recovers P in G1 with e(P,Q)=z with probability at least 39/100 over the challenge and fresh uniform algorithm coins. The bound is worst-case over inputs given the coins: at most 7486945464191340615970310450630709904145664 scalar AArch64 instruction-equivalents, i.e. 7486945464191340615970310450630709904145664/20000 dense-Fp12-multiplication equivalents under C=20000. log2 of that quantity, rounded upward to six decimal places, is 128137645/1000000. Peak memory is 185569945715879859593945323988805046015808 bytes, log2 rounded upward 137091015/1000000. Preprocessing, included in the total, is 3734308784159063841211492322243855087587712 instruction-equivalents, log2 rounded upward 127134109/1000000. Nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. No heuristic, random oracle, quantum step, or uncharged table is used. A hard cap makes the instruction bound independent of how many fingerprint matches occur.

experiments.purpose: Exhaustively check additive BSGS on a small cyclic group, and recheck the integer success inequality and instruction total published in proof.md. This does not establish production curve behavior.
